sources.title: Economic Rescue Plan — official policy page and 36-page download
sources.date: Published 26 October 2026; checked against official launch
sources.finding: Official policy page links the 36-page plan. Text checked against supplied version, including the £1,300 foreword, 64 measures and p.30 in-house model/phasing. Not a byte-for-byte identity claim.

sources.title: Economic Rescue Plan — official PDF download
sources.finding: Official 36-page PDF; printed pp.22 and 31 contain the financial tables, p.30 names an in-house tax-and-transfer model. Published totals do not themselves provide a reproducible model.

sources.title: “Britain is broke, but Britain isn’t beaten”: Reform UK unveils SIXTY-FOUR pro-growth measures to get Britain moving
sources.finding: Official launch dates the plan to 26 October 2026 and describes 64 measures. Confirms provenance of the publisher-hosted version, not independent verification of its costings.

sources.title: Ten better tax cuts than Reform’s £14bn overtime gimmick
sources.finding: Central estimate about £14bn including roughly £4bn static,£7bn relabelling and£3bn PSC arbitrage, less £0.2bn NICs. Earlier proposal/vintage than October plan; not a like-for-like independently certified costing of the final package. Conditional £75,000 hard-cutoff example illustrates a cliff edge.

sources.title: Electricity prices
sources.finding: Jarvis, Levell and Upton: taxes/levies excluding VAT were 17% of average household electricity bill July–October 2026, not 17% of combined gas and electricity. Policy costs real alongside exposure to global gas.

sources.publisher: House of Commons Energy Security and Net Zero Committee
sources.title: The cost of energy
sources.finding: Wholesale electricity price is set most of the time by gas; report recommends reducing policy costs. Supports a multi-cause explanation, not attributing every price change to Net Zero.

sources.title: CBAM definitive regime
sources.date: Undated live guidance; regime from 1 January 2026
sources.finding: EU CBAM definitive regime operates from 1 January 2026; EU importers carry certificate obligations and a verified carbon price paid abroad can reduce the charge, subject to rules. UK exporters face commercial effects rather than automatic direct legal liability.

sources.title: Factsheet: Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)
sources.finding: Section 11 describes May 2025 agreement to work towards UK–EU ETS linkage and mutual CBAM exemptions subject to agreement provisions; not evidence of a completed exemption.

sources.title: Policy FAQs
sources.finding: FAQ says settled status retained while welfare entitlement withdrawn. Establishes party position, not legal compatibility.

sources.title: Implementation of section 45 of the Border Security, Asylum and Immigration Act 2025
sources.finding: Explains current UK-law deeming of citizens’ rights for EUSS status holders, including an extra cohort. Distinguish rights conferred by UK law from everyone independently falling within treaty personal scope.

sources.title: Guidance on the social security coordination provisions of Part 2 of the EU Withdrawal Agreement
sources.finding: Chapter 2, paragraphs 43–45: Article 23 national equal treatment with limited exceptions and Article 24 worker social/tax advantages. Supports legal-compatibility questions for protected people; does not establish proposed levy or citizenship rule is unlawful.

sources.title: Reform UK’s plan for welfare: IFS response
sources.finding: Assessment of August welfare package: around £50bn annual cuts almost entirely from working-age bill just over £200bn in 2030/31; previous tougher disability assessments saved less than expected. Different vintage from October plan; not independent scoring of every final line.

sources.title: Spending pressures, not fiscal headroom, are the Chancellor’s key Budget challenge
sources.finding: Higher interest rates add around £10bn to borrowing in 2029/30 versus March baseline, while other effects can offset this. Not an extra deduction from Reform’s margin: its plan already adjusts interest rates.

sources.title: How much is Universal Credit?
sources.finding: Earnings taper applies after income tax and National Insurance, above any work allowance; supports conditional own arithmetic £486×55%=£267.30 less UC and £218.70 net gain, not a full household simulation.

sources.title: Public funds: accessible guidance
sources.finding: EUSS settled-status section states benefit access is on the same basis as British citizens or other settled people, subject to normal eligibility. Describes current law, not a ruling on a future policy.

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme (UK ETS): a policy overview
sources.finding: Current overview says UK and EU are negotiating ETS linkage; negotiations are not a completed agreement or automatic mutual CBAM exemption.
